_incident:
A decommissioned 33kV switching compound on hard standing: an access road and gate line along the south, a relay building, a marshalling kiosk, five switch bays in a row across the north, a scrap compound, an oil bund on the north-east corner and a busbar gantry line down the middle. The load-bearing fact is that it is OUTDOORS AND BUILT, which is neither of the two arguments this build already has.

THE THREE SHIPPED MAPS ARE THREE POSITIONS ON ONE QUESTION: how much of what you can see stops the thing? The cold store is almost entirely fence and four shelving runs are the exception. Blackthorn is the inverse — 441.8m of deer fence, chain-link and tree line against 49.5m of concrete, 10.1%, and not one square metre of it fenced bare. This compound is the third position and it is not a midpoint: 226.4m of cast concrete against 379.6m of palisade, chain-link, lattice and steel cladding, which is 37.4% of the built length — and the concrete IS NOT DISTRIBUTED. It is six enclosures, and every one of them opens the same way.

SO THIS SITE HANDS A SQUAD MORE READY-MADE CONTAINMENT THAN ANY MAP IN THE BUILD AND EVERY BIT OF IT FACES SOUTH. Measured with the real `isFenced`, every door shut and nothing deployed: a switch bay reads 3 escape rays of 24 at the back and 11 in its own mouth; the oil bund reads 3; the relay room with its door shut reads 1, because its cable-way opening is the only hole in it. Against that, the open centre yard is 23, hard against the palisade is 20, the scrap compound — which looks exactly like a pen and is chain-link — is 19, and the access road is 18. There is no position on this compound worth having that is not already a room.

AND THE PRICES ARE ALL DIFFERENT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF HAVING SIX. A bay mouth is 3.6m: one 2.4m barrier panel leaves 1 ray open, two panels close it, two floodlights close it, and ONE portable heater closes it on its own because a heater's 40C contour is 3.066m of radius at this ambient and a floodlight's is 1.687m. The bund mouth is 2.6m, so one panel closes it and so does one floodlight — the only enclosure on the site that a single long-slot item shuts. The relay room needs one panel over the cable-way and the yard circuit up to shut its door. Open ground still costs four floodlights inside 1.9m, exactly as it does on the reserve. So the cheapest pen on the compound is the bund, and the bund is the far corner.

INFRASTRUCTURE BUYS LIGHT AND ALMOST NOTHING ELSE. 34.6% of standable ground has any illumination on arrival — four emergency fittings and nothing else — against 98.9% with both circuits live. On 32 metres of grey chippings in the dark that is the difference between a compound you can search and one you cannot. The two breakers are deliberately in different halves: the yard incomer is inside the relay building and the bay circuit is on the marshalling kiosk out in the open, so restoring the site is a walk rather than a switch.

THE ONE THING THE COMPOUND GIVES AWAY IS THE WAY IN. The vehicle gate is on the yard circuit and is shut and dead on arrival, and it does not matter: the inner chain-link fence is 3.4m short at its east end and has been since the scrap compound was opened up. Driven, that detour is 14.7s of walking. Everything else on this site is reachable with every door on the map shut.
_webNote:
Authored for the browser build against revision 0.4.0-web of the equipment manifest. Pure geometry: no `anomalySpawn`, no `evidenceSources`, no `instanceSites`. The incident supplies all three and `validateMap` runs on the merged document.

BOUNDS ARE 32m BY 32m, AND THAT SIZE IS A RECOMMENDATION THIS MAP IS TAKING UP. `blackthorn-reserve`'s own note records that `ThermalFloor` samples a fixed 96x96 grid whatever the bounds are, so a 48m map is 0.5000 m/px and loses three quarters of the contour a 24m map draws — and it ends by recommending that any future outdoor map wanting a lit fence be authored at 32m or 40m rather than 48m. MEASURED here: 0.3333 m/px, 1.85x coarser than the rule's own 0.18m path sampling (so the picture still never promises a gap the rule does not resolve), and a lone floodlight's 40C disc covers 80 of the 9,216 thermal-floor pixels against 20 on a 48m map. This compound's fence can be made of heat and the imager can still draw it.

MARK_RANGE_M IS 30m AND THE DIAGONAL IS 45.3m, so a squad that splits still loses part of the ping board, and `pressure.withdrawalDistanceM` is 14m, which is reachable here and is not on a 24m floor.

CEILING HEIGHT IS 5.2m AND IT IS A COMPROMISE, NOT A MEASUREMENT — the same compromise `blackthorn-reserve` records for the same reason. `scene.js` draws a ceiling plane over the whole bounds and hangs every mains luminaire at h - 0.25 with a distance-9 point light, so an open sky would leave the yard unlit. 5.2m reads as open air under the exponential fog and still puts the fittings within reach of the ground. Porous statics render as open racking at a fixed 2.6m regardless, which is why the palisade, the chain-link, the gantry legs and the steel cladding read as see-through and the concrete does not.

MEASURED, by driving the real Site, HeatField, DeployableSet, Anomaly and ThermalFloor against this file. Every figure below is produced by section A or B of tools/content-tests.js.

Geometry. 41 statics, no two overlapping; no door rect overlapping a static or another door; 17 room rects, none overlapping; no crate inside a static; no luminaire fitting buried in one. Clearance at every anchor with EVERY DOOR SHUT, against the 0.34m operative radius: spawn 2.400, cache 2.200, extraction 2.400, yard breaker 1.000, bay breaker 0.600 — worst 0.600m, and the four-operative 1.1m spawn ring is clear. On a 0.20m grid there are 18,827 standable cells and all 18,827 of them are reachable from the spawn with every door on the map shut; the gate and the two other doors are shortcuts, never gates on the only way through. `roomNameAt` names every one of those cells, no cell reports "Unmarked floor", every one of the 17 authored rooms is reached by some standable cell, and the worst distance from a standable cell to the rect that names it is 0.100m.

Built length. 226.4m insulating against 379.6m porous — 37.4% of the built length of this compound stops a mass and 100% of it stops a person. With every door shut it presents 50 rects that stop a person and 28 that stop a mass.

Fences, bare, doors shut, nothing deployed: bay 3 at the back 3 of 24, bay 3 in its own mouth 11, bay 1 at the back 3, oil bund at the back 3, relay room with its door shut 1, scrap compound 19, open centre yard 23, hard against the palisade 20, back road 13, access road 18. Deployed: bay 3 with one panel across the mouth 1, with two panels 0, with two floodlights 0, with one heater 0; the bund with one panel 0 and with one floodlight 0; open yard with four floodlights inside 1.9m 0.

Light. 34.6% of standable ground has any mains illumination with nothing energised, 69.5% on the yard circuit, 72.3% on the bay circuit, 98.9% on both.
_extractionNote:
GDD §26.2 asks for two routes out and the map format's `extraction` field is one point, so this map ships one point and two ways to reach it. The point is the vehicle on the access road at (-9.6, -13.6) radius 2.0, beside the spawn and the cargo cache and south of the inner fence. The compound proper is separated from the road by a chain-link line at z = -11.2 to -10.8 which is crossed in exactly two places: the VEHICLE GATE at x = -7.4 to -4.4, powered off the yard circuit and shut and dead on arrival, and the 3.4m the fence is permanently short at its east end, x = 12.6 to 16.0, which has no door in it and never has. Measured on the shipped geometry with every door shut: every one of the 18,827 standable cells is still reachable from the spawn, which is the proof that the east gap is a real route rather than a scenic one, and the walk from the gate line round the east end and back into the middle of the yard costs 14.7s of sim time. Restoring the yard circuit is what opens the gate and turns that into a straight line.

The two doors inside the compound are shortcuts on the same principle. The relay building has a powered door on its south face and a permanent cable-way opening 1.6m wide on its east, so its breaker can always be reached; the scrap compound has a powered gate in its north fence and is open on its west side, so the skip can always be reached. Neither door is ever the only way to anything, which is why both of them are on this incident's route-jamming list and the vehicle gate is not.
_porousNote:
Indices into `statics` that stop a PERSON and not a mass. On this compound the line is drawn at CAST CONCRETE, and it is drawn by the order of the array: 0 to 24 are every square metre of this site that stops something the way a barrier panel does, and 25 to 40 are everything else. Read the first twenty-five and you have read every enclosure the site owns.

0 to 5 are the relay building — two south-wall segments with the door between them, the north wall, the west wall, and two east-wall segments with a permanent 1.6m cable-way opening between them. 6 is the marshalling kiosk, a solid block with the bay breaker on its east face. 7 to 21 are the five switch bays, three rects each: a back wall and two returns, mouths 3.6m wide and all five facing south in a row. 22 to 24 are the oil bund, three sides of a 4.6m by 2.6m cell open to the west. Six enclosures, twenty-five runs, 226.4m.

Everything from 25 is porous, and that is 379.6m: the compound's own boundary is palisade on all four sides (25-28), the inner line between the road and the yard is chain-link with a 3.4m gap at its east end (29-30), the busbar gantry is five steel lattice legs a person walks round and nothing else does not (31-35), the scrap compound is chain-link on three sides with a gate in the north (36-39), and 40 is the steel-clad store hut on the west margin. 37.4% of the built length of this compound stops a mass and 100% of it stops a person — which is neither the cold store, where the building's own structure IS the fence, nor Blackthorn, where 10.1% of it is.

Two consequences worth stating because both are ways to lose an operation. A closed DOOR is always insulated — `Site._rebuildBlocking` pushes a shut door into `insulatedRects` unconditionally and there is no porous door — so the scrap compound's north gate is 2.4m of insulation in a chain-link fence and shutting it on something achieves nothing at all. And CRATES are not insulation either: `Site` puts them in `_blocking` and never in `_insulatedStatics`, so the six of them here are cover for a person and nothing to a mass. With every door shut this compound presents 50 rects that stop a person and 28 that stop a mass.
